dedupe_keys.name: cash usage database share of cash in consumer payments 35 countries

description: The Cash Usage Database compiles the share of cash in consumer transactions by volume and by value across countries, drawn from payment diary studies and other central bank and industry assessments. The workbook read on the Mendeley Data page has one row per country and study year with ISO2 code, country name, year, cash share by volume, cash share by value, the institution that ran the survey (such as the European Central Bank, Bank of Korea or UK Finance), a source citation and a link; its readme says it now covers 35 countries and 193 observations from 1996 to 2026, was last updated on 10 September 2026, and is meant to be updated twice a year. Version 3 was published on 17 September 2026 by Kotkowski, Dybka, Piotrowska and Van Hove as one Excel workbook of about 30 KB, downloadable and free under CC BY 4.0, citing their 2025 SGH Warsaw School of Economics working paper. Coverage is mostly Europe plus Australia, Canada, Chile, the Philippines, South Africa, South Korea, Thailand, Türkiye and the United States. Caveats: survey methods differ by country, some surveys ask only about the most recent payment, and years are uneven. For simulation it sets how much everyday spending depends on cash, not card and digital rails, a key input for scenarios of payment system outages, power cuts and cash access loss. Related catalogue records include the FCA access to cash coverage data, the ECB payments statistics and the BIS CPMI Red Book payment statistics.
